newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India sits on hands, waits direction.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India sits on hands, waits direction.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) traded in London ended little changed after bid/offer spreads were widened in morning trade due to nervousness over the outlook for the local market.
As Bombay demonstrated some resilience, spreads narrowed and the market closed little changed, although the market premium came in to from Friday's 9.94 percent to 7.90 percent on Monday.
"There was little trading in the market today, no buying pressure and after the start, little selling pressure," said a trader.
The James Capel Indian GDR Index rose 0.16 points, or 0.25 percent, to 65.03 points.
"Some premiums are under big pressure here," said one trader, "Some of the less liquid stocks such as Sanghi Polyester and Crompton Greaves were badly hit in morning trade."
The Indian market has been in the doldrums for some time, but a took a new turn down last week after news that ex-Prime Minister Narasimha Rao was charged in a bribery case.

Elsewhere in Asia, Taiwan ended little changed, with the Capel Taiwan Index up 0.35 points, 0.39 percent, to 89.93 points, a premium of 2.31 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index ended 3.49 points down at 6,504.68.
The Capel Korea Index fell 2.25 points, 3.1 percent to 70.33 points, a premium of 30.24 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index ended down 3.54 points at a provisional 789.67.
The Korean market opening takes effect from Tuesday and raises the foreign limit on shareholdings to 20 percent from 18 percent. --David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
